text:
maya: Quick experiment — trying a "compact index" that coalesces small safetensors shards into bundle pages to reduce S3 head/GET overhead. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/weights/compare/compact-index

rio: Nice. Main question: how do we keep atomicity? If we coalesce, can we still hot-swap a single layer?

maya: Plan: store an index sidecar mapping logical shard -> bundle id + byte range. Bundles are append-only; we publish a new bundle and atomically swap index. That keeps hot-swap at index level.

sam: Two concerns: 1) cache invalidation when index swap happens. 2) warmup: we often prefetch hot shards — how do we avoid re-downloading large bundles for small evictions?

maya: For (1) we version the index (index_vN.json) and use ETag-based fetch + compare. For (2) we want a "sub-range fetch" path via range requests; also a small-file fastpath: if shard < 64KB keep separate.

jin: Range requests cost more on some providers and hurts latency. Also partial reads mean we may keep lots of tiny pinned mmaps; eviction complexity increases.

sam: Could we use a lightweight manifest that lists hot offsets so warmup can ask for only those offsets? Example manifest:
```
{
  "bundle": "bundle-2024-05-10",
  "hot_ranges": [
    {"start": 1024, "end": 32768},
    {"start": 65536, "end": 131072}
  ]
}
```

rio: That helps warmup but doesn't solve atomic swap ordering. We need a rollout plan: canary index, fallback to original manifest, and a verifier that checks checksums.

maya: Agreed. Proposed rollout: 1) publish bundle + index_vN; 2) canary nodes pull index_vN for 10% traffic; 3) run checksum verifier against sample hotwarmsets; 4) if ok, promote and update alias "current_index" -> index_vN.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout started for index_vN on cluster-ml-canary :rocket:

jin: Also add metric: bundle_miss_bytes and range_request_count. If range_request_count spikes, we revert.

sam: Implementation detail: loader API change: accept either {"type":"direct","url":...} or {"type":"bundle","bundle_id":...,"range":...}. Keep loader interface backward-compatible.

maya: Good. I'll draft the loader shim. Action items: sam=load-test for bundle warmup throughput; jin=eviction model + metrics; rio=write rollout checklist. I'll open PR and link there.

rio: tl;dr: promising but watch partial-read latencies and eviction complexity. Happy with plan to prototype.

maya: thanks folks :thumbsup:
